title: Braking distance calculation
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly compute the minimum braking distance using the kinematic equation v_t^2 - v_0^2 = 2a_1 x_1, yielding 108 m.

title: Total process time
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly sum the deceleration and acceleration times (t1 + t2) to find the minimum total time, yielding 10 s.

title: Time delay determination
description: Essential Criteria: The student must correctly compute the time delay by subtracting the uniform-motion time (total distance/v0) from the total process time, yielding 4 s.

title: Kinematic equation application
description: Important Criteria: The student must apply the correct kinematic equations (time-dependent and time-independent) for both deceleration and acceleration phases.

title: Acceleration distance calculation
description: Important Criteria: The student must compute the acceleration distance using v_0^2 - v_t^2 = 2a_2 x_2, which is needed for the time delay analysis.

title: Sign convention consistency
description: Pitfall Criteria: The student incorrectly assigns signs to acceleration/deceleration (e.g., treating deceleration as positive acceleration) in the kinematic equations.

title: Unit omission or mismatch
description: Pitfall Criteria: The student provides numerical answers without proper units (m, s) or uses inconsistent units in calculations.

title: Alternative solution check
description: Optional Criteria: The student verifies the time delay by comparing the area under a velocity-time graph to the uniform-motion case.
